sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Differences of the alate from closely related species: in N. angusticeps the head, pronotum and frontal gland plate are smaller, the pronotum is densely covered with long hairs, the compound eyes and ocelli are larger, the ocelli are closer to the compound eyes, and the forewing is shorter; in N. bodkini the compound eyes and ocelli are larger, the ocelli are closer to the compound eyes, the forewing is shorter and narrower, and the tibial spur formula is 2:2:2; in N. taracua the head is narrower, the ocelli are larger and closer to the compound eyes, and the pronotum is narrower; the alate of N. braziliensis is much smaller than this species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown with a reddish tinge, with a narrow paler ring around the frontal gland plate; postclypeus paler than the rest of the head; mandibles pale yellow with black apices; mouthparts, legs and antennae straw-coloured; pronotum slightly darker than the meso- and metanota; wing scales light brown; abdominal segments coloured as the pronotum (colour variation considerable: some specimens dark brown, with trochanters and femora pale yellow and tibiae and tarsi light brown; some males are also rather dark, with trochanters and femora pure yellow). The head bears a few longer, fine, erect setae, and the postclypeus a few additional short setae; the pronotum and legs bear numerous long and medium-length fine curved setae; the meso- and metanota are much more sparsely hairy; the wing scales bear numerous long fine setae; the abdominal tergites and sternites are densely covered with curved setae of unequal size. In profile the upper margin of the head is undulate, sloping slightly downwards from the frontal gland plate towards the anterior margin, the disc slightly convex, the frontal gland plate pear-shaped, flat, lying in a shallow circular depression. Compound eyes bulging, nearly circular, the upper margin slightly angular. Ocelli semicircular above, the lower margin fairly straight. Antennae 17-segmented, segment 4 the shortest, slightly shorter than segment 3, segment 5 twice segment 4 and slightly shorter than segment 6, segments 7 and 8 about equal, segments 9 and 10 about equal and slightly longer than segment 8, segments 11 to 16 gradually decreasing in length, segment 17 elongate-oval, as long as the penultimate segment. Pronotum mostly flat, slightly concave near the anterior lateral corners, the anterior margin slightly concave, the lateral margins slightly curved, the posterior margin with a very shallow and broad notch in the middle. The posterior margins of the meso- and metanota have a deep, rounded notch, and the posterior corners project slightly but are not sharp. Measurements (mm, range): head length in profile 1.22—1.33; head width (including compound eyes) 1.79—1.94; compound eye diameter 0.46—0.49; distance between the lower margins of the compound eyes 0.10; ocellus long diameter 0.14—0.15; ocellus short diameter 0.10; ocellus to compound eye distance 0.13—0.14; frontal gland plate length 0.20; pronotal maximum length 0.92—1.02; pronotal midline length 0.89—0.97; pronotal maximum width 1.53—1.58; hind tibia length 2.14—2.19; forewing length from the suture 14.40—14.80; forewing width 4.10—4.30.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head straw-coloured; the anterior margin of the head, mouthparts, antennae, postmental suture and frontal line brownish; mandibles shining black except for the brown base; pronotum and legs pale yellow; abdomen milky white. The dorsal surface of the head bears numerous sparse, fine, erect setae and the ventral surface is hairless; the submentum has 2 stout marginal setae at each anterolateral corner; the disc of the labrum bears a few erect setae, and the apex of the midlobe has about 4 longer, fine setae; the anterior surface of the pronotum is covered with very short and sparse setae, the margin of the anterior lobe has a row of minute hairs, and the posterior surface bears numerous sparse, long, stiff setae, very sparse on the posterior lobe; the legs are almost hairless, with a row of hairs of unequal length along the longitudinal ridge, and a few more on the surface of the fore coxa; the cervical sclerites are bare. Head elongate, nearly square, 1.70—1.78 times as long as wide and 1.20—1.30 times as long as the left mandible, with parallel sides, slightly constricted at the antennal insertions; the vertex is straight in profile, slightly concave at the frontal gland, with another slightly larger depression behind the frons; the lower side is slightly undulate and somewhat depressed. Antennae 16-segmented, segments 3 and 4 about equal and the shortest, segments 5 to 11 gradually increasing in length, segments 12 to 15 decreasing more abruptly, segment 16 elongate-oval and longer than the preceding segment. Labrum well developed, its left side almost straight, the right side broadly arcuate, the anterior margin with 3 small, regular lobes. Mandibles slightly shorter than the head. The left mandible is broadly curved at the basal third, then straight, then concave to the swollen apex. The right mandible is almost straight in profile, only the apical quarter bent downwards, the upper surface concave as a shallow groove along the inner margin, the apex narrowed to a short but rather sharp point. Submentum long (equal to 0.6 of the head length), with little expansion at the two ends (constriction index 0.5), its sides very gently and broadly concave, the anterior margin straight and the posterior margin broadly concave. Pronotum equal to 0.64 of the head width, its two lobes forming an angle slightly greater than a right angle, the anterior lobe semicircular with a regular notch in the middle, the posterior lobe with slightly curved sides and a shallowly concave posterior margin in the middle. Mesonotum narrow, transverse, with a broad concavity on the disc. The anterior margin of the metanotum descends steeply to receive the posterior margin of the mesonotum, and its posterior margin is very broadly and deeply concave, so that the metanotum forms two arched lateral lobes joined by a narrow waist. The mid tibia bears 1 or 2 spines, slightly stouter than ordinary setae.
